# Intent Statement — Simple React Todo App

## Sources

- [desc] Initial description: "Build a simple React todo app"
- [scope] Workflow-selected scope: `feature`.
- [Q1] Business problem: personal task tracking.
- [Q2] Customer: individual end users managing their own personal tasks.
- [Q3] Success: users can add, complete, and delete todos reliably.
- [Q4] Trigger: personal need / opportunity.
- [Q5] Decision-maker: the developer alone decides scope and priorities.
- [Q6] Communication: informal, no reporting needed.
- [Q7] Confirmed product boundary: a self-contained todo feature (add, toggle, delete todos).

## Problem Statement

Individuals need a simple way to keep track of the things they have to do. [Q1]
This initiative delivers a lightweight personal todo application so a single
user can capture tasks, mark them done, and remove them without friction. [Q1] [Q7]

## Target Customer

The intended user is an individual end user managing their own personal
tasks. [Q2] The application is single-user and personal in nature; it is not
aimed at teams or external product customers. [Q2] [Q5]

## Success Metrics

Success is defined functionally: the user can reliably add a todo, mark a todo
complete (and reverse it), and delete a todo. [Q3] The measurable outcome is
that each of these three actions works correctly and predictably every time
the user performs it. [Q3] [Q7]

## Initiative Trigger

The work is driven by a personal need or opportunity rather than external
pressure such as regulation or a market deadline. [Q4]

## Initial Scope Signal

- **Workflow-selected scope:** `feature` (workflow-selected). [scope]
- **User-confirmed product boundary:** a self-contained personal todo feature
  supporting adding, toggling completion of, and deleting todos. [Q7]

The user confirmed that the workflow-selected `feature` scope matches the
intended product boundary. [Q7]

## Assumptions & Open Questions

None.
